definition: An organic-rich, solid microbiological culture medium that contains (beef) heart infusion and tryptose.  Used to grow a wide range of heterotrophic microorganisms.
definition source:
From: Heart Infusion Agar (Becton-Dickinson Difco and BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media, 2nd edition):

Intended Use
Heart Infusion Agar is a general-purpose medium used in the cultivation of a wide range of microorganisms from a variety of clinical and nonclinical specimens.

Principles of the Procedure
Heart Infusion Agar derives its nutrients from heart muscle infusion and peptone, which supply nitrogenous and carbonaceous compounds, sulfur, vitamins and trace ingredients. Sodium chloride maintains osmotic equilibrium. Agar is the solidifying agent. The addition of 5% sheep blood provides additional growth factors and is used to determine hemolytic reactions.

Formula
Difco™ Heart Infusion Agar
Approximate Formula* Per Liter
Beef Heart, Infusion from 500 g................................. 10.0 g
Tryptose..................................................................... 10.0 g
Sodium Chloride.......................................................... 5.0 g
Agar.......................................................................... 15.0 g
*Adjusted and/or supplemented as required to meet performance criteria.

pH 7.4 ± 0.2
